title: KV cache warmup & cold-start throughput prober with phasic workload matrix
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a reproducible benchmarking harness that exercise KV/prefix cache behavior across distinct lifecycle phases: cold-start, warmup, steady-state, and controlled eviction. The harness must produce time-series of tokens/sec, p95 latency, hit-rate, and memory footprint for configurable workloads, and feed a nightly regression detection job. Goals: characterize warmup cost, identify worst-case cold-start p95, quantify tokens/sec improvement as hit-rate rises, and catch regressions in both throughput and tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run deterministic phasic scenarios (cold -> warm -> steady -> eviction) with seedable workload generator
Output artifact includes per-phase time-series of tokens/sec, p95, hit_rate, mem_rss_mb, and request_mix breakdown
Nightly regression job ingests artifacts and flags >10% tokens/sec drop or >20% p95 increase for a canonical profile
Grafana dashboard showing heatmap of hit-rate vs p95 vs memory with selectable model/sequence length
End-to-end test and CI job added; PR merged with docs linking to confluence and dashboard
test_plan: Phasic workloads: cold-start (0 warm keys), rapid suffix traffic to simulate first-request heavy workloads
Warmup ramp: synthetic traces that incrementally increase prefix reuse to sweep hit-rate from 0% to 95%
Eviction stress: fixed memory budget with periodic large unique-key bursts to trigger eviction and measure tail latency
Steady-state throughput: constant QPS runs at different batching configs to map tokens/sec vs p95
Regression detection: nightly compare against baseline artifacts with tolerance parameters stored in S3

comments: Aisha Kumar (2026-02-17): Initial notes — we should prioritize reproducibility across machine families (A100 vs H100) and ensure kernel selection variability is captured in metadata.

Jonah Reed (2026-02-23): Prototype looks good. Trade-off: running full phasic matrix across all model sizes is very expensive. Proposal: canonical set of 3 representatives (small/med/large) and stratified sampling for others.
Priya Singh (2026-03-01): UX ask — include a compact summary CSV with per-phase aggregates for quick onboarding by SRE and PMs.
Ben Torres (SRE, 2026-03-05): Observed noisy p95 when host has background eviction; recommend isolating bench hosts or tagging runs and filtering noisy hosts in analysis step.
Jonah Reed (2026-03-09): Regression job produced one false positive due to config drift (batching config mismatch). Added config hash to artifact and require match for nightly compare.
notes: Be intentional about run isolation: noisy co-tenancy leads to spurious p95 variance. Use dedicated bench nodes when possible.
We observed that hit-rate improvements have nonlinear benefits on tokens/sec due to batching windows — capture batching stats per-sample.
Future work: extend the harness to simulate multi-tenant traffic mixes and test smart-routing fallbacks.
Keep artifacts immutable and sign them (SHA256) to avoid regression flapping due to artifact replacement.
